## 1. Exact theorem

Let \(\rho_N\) be permutation invariant and have the exact maximally-mixed-input Schur weights \(w_{N,M}\) displayed in growing_relative_entropy.md. Let \(\tau=\rho_{N,1}=(I+b\cdot\sigma)/2\), and write \(\rho_r=\rho_{N,r}\). For \(1\le r\le N/1024\),
\[
 \boxed{\chi^2_{\rm P}(\rho_r\|\tau^{\otimes r})
 :=\operatorname{Tr}[\rho_r^2(\tau^{\otimes r})^{-1}]-1
 \le 2\cdot10^9(r/N)^2,}
\]
and hence
\[
 \boxed{D(\rho_r\|\tau^{\otimes r})\le2\cdot10^9(r/N)^2.}
\]
The constant is intentionally loose. Every subextensive sequence \(r_N=o(N)\) satisfies the size restriction eventually. The theorem holds uniformly over arbitrary states inside each conserved Schur sector, so it holds at all times/occupations of the specified collective bath. For \(r=1\), the quantities are exactly zero rather than merely bounded.

The reference \(\tau^{\otimes N}\) is fully separable and exactly matches all one-body data. It generally DOES NOT have the target's conserved Casimir or Schur law. Thus its use as a hard alternative requires soundness against the unrestricted fully separable set. A trusted promise that the null has the same Casimir changes the certification problem and is treated separately below.

## 2. Weighted centered basis and the support-wise conditioning issue

Set \(B_a=\sigma_a-b_aI\). Under the one-qubit inner product
\(\langle A,C\rangle_\tau=\operatorname{Tr}\tau A^\dagger C\), these operators are orthogonal to the identity and have Gram matrix
\[
 G_{ab}=\delta_{ab}-b_ab_b+i\epsilon_{abk}b_k.
\]
Its eigenvalues are \(1-|b|,1+|b|,1-|b|^2\). The conserved Casimir implies
\[
 |b|^2=4|\langle J\rangle|^2/N^2\le3/N,
\]
so \(\tau\) is full rank and \(G\succeq(1-|b|)I\succeq I/2\) for the stated range.

For the product reference \(T=\tau^{\otimes r}\), let \(L=\rho_rT^{-1}\). Then
\(\|L\|_T^2=\operatorname{Tr}\rho_r^2T^{-1}\). Its coefficient against a product of centered basis operators on support \(S\) is exactly
\[
 \langle B_S,L\rangle_T=\operatorname{Tr}\rho_r B_S^\dagger.
\]
The last equality uses cyclicity to cancel the adjacent \(T^{-1}T\); it does not assume \(\rho_r\) commutes with \(T\). Orthogonal decomposition by supports and finite-dimensional Parseval give
\[
 \chi^2_{\rm P}
 =\sum_{S\ne\varnothing} C_S^\dagger(G^{-1})^{\otimes|S|}C_S
 \le\sum_{w=2}^r2^w\sum_{|S|=w}\sum_{a_1,\ldots,a_w}|C_{a_1\ldots a_w}|^2.
\]

INDEPENDENT WHITE-SECTOR LOCAL PURITY THEOREM
Agent: /root/marginal_blind
Session: 01a11aeb-d321-71e3-a5ef-ecd7e0e32bae
Agent thread: 01a11af1-8374-7e23-8606-3340a0da2731
This is a new independent proof after FROZEN_REPORT.txt was frozen. That
original report has not been changed. No thermal derivation or other agent
derivation was read. No descendants were spawned.

EXACT THEOREM

Let rho_N be any permutation-invariant N-qubit state with exactly the
maximally mixed Schur-Weyl sector weights

 rho_N = direct_sum_j p_j rho_j tensor I_(m_j)/m_j,
 p_j=(2j+1)m_j/2^N, Tr rho_j=1,
 m_j=binomial(N,N/2-j)-binomial(N,N/2-j-1).

The matrices rho_j can be arbitrary density matrices in their spin-j spaces.
Let rho_r be any r-qubit marginal, tau_r=I/2^r, and q=r/N. Define the white
reference chi-square quantity by

 chi2(rho_r||tau_r)=2^r Tr(rho_r^2)-1.

For 1<=r<=N with q<1/2,

 chi2(rho_r||tau_r)
 <= 108 q(1+3q)/(1-2q)^(7/2).                             (A)

In particular, for r<=N/128,

 chi2(rho_r||tau_r) <= 128 r/N.                            (B)

The constants here are uniform in N,r and all choices of rho_j. This proves
the requested claim with substantially smaller C than 50000. No dynamical
solution, positivity of a coherent-state representation, finite de Finetti
approximation, or assumption of sector extremizer purity is used.

The proof is a Pauli-degree expansion plus a one-variable polynomial bound.

STEP 1: AN ELEMENTARY POLYNOMIAL GRID LEMMA

For every real polynomial P of degree at most k>=1, and any nonnegative
integer or half-integer j, the spin grid G_j={-j,-j+1,...,j} obeys

 max_(m in G_j) P(m)^2
 <= 36 k^2 (1/(2j+1)) sum_(m in G_j) P(m)^2.              (C)

If j<4k^2 this is immediate, since 2j+1<=9k^2. Otherwise let
M=max_(x in [-j,j]) |P(x)|. The classical Markov polynomial derivative
inequality, rescaled to [-j,j], is

 max |P'| <= (k^2/j) M.

At a point x_* attaining M, all points in the intersection of [-j,j] with
[x_*-j/(2k^2),x_*+j/(2k^2)] have |P(x)|>=M/2. This intersection has length
at least j/(2k^2)>=2, and contains at least j/(4k^2) spin-grid points. Thus
sum_m P(m)^2 >= j M^2/(16k^2). Since j>=4k^2>=4,
(2j+1)/j<=9/4, proving (C) with constant 36. The case j=0 was already
covered by the elementary small-grid case.
